Subject: Quick clarifications — VPC storage residency & deletion evidence

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — the team liked the latency numbers. Before we proceed to procurement, Legal and Infrastructure have a few pointed questions about Private/VPC deployments:

1) When we select "customer-controlled storage" behind a VPC, can you confirm what data (model checkpoints, logs, activation traces, cached prompts/KV) will remain in our storage vs Redwood-managed control plane? We need a bulletized mapping similar to what you showed but in writing.

2) On deletion: if we request a tenant wipe, what is the timeline for (a) logical deletion, (b) background snapshots/backup expiration, and (c) cryptographic sanitization of encryption keys? Do you provide a signed attestation or report we can store?

3) Evidence: will Redwood provide proof-of-delete artifacts (e.g., job receipts, snapshot purge logs, KMS key rotation/expiry records) that we can attach to our compliance package? If so, what format and retention will those artifacts have?

Attaching our security questionnaire (partial) to make it easier — Legal would prefer concrete answers we can quote in the SOW.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (serving/runtime) for the technical breakdown and Rishi for the attestation/contract language. Below is a short written summary; Dev will follow with the operational details and exact artifact types we can provide.

High-level (summary):
- Customer-controlled storage (VPC data plane): customer tenant data — generated requests, cached KV, and persisted model artifacts placed in customer-managed object storage buckets — remain in your account/project unless you request transfer.
- Redwood control plane: metadata (route configs, billing counters, orchestration state) is stored in Redwood-managed systems but is logically separated and never contains raw prompt/content blobs for customer VPC deployments.
- Deletion timeline: logical delete (mark + revoke access) within 24 hours of request; background snapshot purges on standard cadence (30–90 days depending on snapshot policy) unless a rapid purge is requested under SOW; KMS key zeroization/rotation logged and can be correlated to the wipe window.
- Evidence: we can produce purge job receipts, object-delete event lists, and KMS key lifecycle logs. Rishi — can you confirm attestation format we can produce for SOW?

Next: Dev — can you provide the artifact types and an example timeline (hours / days) for a tenant-initiated full wipe on a dedicated VPC deployment (customer-owned buckets + CMK)? Also note any manual steps required by the customer.

Warmly,
Grace
Head of Solutions — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications — VPC storage residency & deletion evidence

Hi all — technical breakdown below. I'll keep it focused and action-oriented so Legal can copy-paste into the SOW.

1) Data mapping (Private/VPC, customer-controlled storage with CMK):
- Customer object storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) in your account: persists tenant artifacts — logs, model snapshots you choose to store, cached KV for warm-starts. Redwood will only write to buckets you configure; by default we create tenant-specific prefixes and tag objects with tenant-id and timestamp.
- Control plane (Redwood-managed): orchestration metadata (task ids, scheduling signals). We do not persist customer plaintext prompts or outputs here for VPC + customer-store configurations — only pointers (object URIs, checksums).
- Ephemeral runtime memory: KV cache and in-memory activations live on serving nodes' RAM and are not persisted unless explicitly flushed to your storage (per your config).

2) Deletion workflow (tenant-initiated full-wipe, customer-storage + CMK):
- Step 1: Request received (API / Console / Signed SOW).
  - Effect: immediate access revoke keys for serving processes to prevent new reads (within 1 hour).
- Step 2: Logical delete & purge job enqueued (within 24 hours).
  - Purge job will delete objects under tenant prefixes and rotate/disable CMK wrapping keys.
- Step 3: Snapshot & backup expiration reconciliation (48–72 hours typical):
  - If any system-level snapshots reference your objects (e.g., cross-region replication snapshots), we schedule dependent deletions and confirm once all references are gone.
- Step 4: Cryptographic sanitization: we rotate and retire CMKs; where HSM-backed keys are customer-controlled, we provide the key destruction/rotation record. Physical secure erase for disks (on-host) follows standard tenancy churn and is recorded in host decommission logs.
- Step 5: Attestation & evidence generation (3–7 days depending on scope):
  - Artifacts: purge job log (JSON list of object URIs + timestamps), object delete events (cloud provider event ids), CMK rotation/destruction records, snapshot reconciliation report, and a signed attestation statement from Redwood.

3) Artifacts & formats:
- Purge job receipts: line-delimited JSON (object_uri, delete_timestamp, delete_event_id).
- Snapshot reconciliation: CSV with snapshot id, region, resolution status.
- KMS/CMK records: provider-native key event ids and rotation timestamps (PDF export available).
- Signed attestation: PDF with summary, scope, and a Redwood signatory + ISO timestamp.

4) Customer actions required:
- Confirm bucket prefixes to be purged (we will not delete objects outside a confirmed prefix).
- If you control CMK, issue a key-destruction confirmation token or authorize Redwood to rotate and retire placeholder wrapping keys (this is documented in the SOW).
- For accelerated purge (under 72 hours), approve expedited ops runbook and cost buffer for out-of-band resource operations.

I'll attach example purge-job JSON and a template attestation in the shared Drive.

—Dev

Redwood Inference
